questions.stem: What is the ΔH value for an endothermic reaction?

options.text: Positive, because energy is absorbed from the surroundings
Zero, because no energy change occurs
It cannot be determined without experimental data

questions.explanation: Endothermic reactions always have a positive ΔH value. This is because the products have more energy than the reactants, meaning energy has been absorbed from the surroundings.

questions.stem: Why does thermal decomposition stop when heating is stopped?

options.text: Because the products have been used up
Because the catalyst has been consumed
Because the reaction is endothermic and requires a continuous supply of energy
Because the reaction reaches equilibrium immediately

questions.explanation: Thermal decomposition is endothermic, meaning it requires a continuous input of energy to proceed. When heating stops, no more energy is supplied, so the reaction cannot continue and stops.
